criteria.note: The strongest criterion in the item, and it is evidenced rather than argued. The four derived fields really are recomputed and not trusted: I drove error_pct_of returning 0 always (8 rows red, including the committed example record on disk, which is the only witness that can catch a builder and a validator agreeing with each other) and outcome_of collapsing to in_range (10 rows red, the widest blast radius in the fragment), each applied to BOTH module copies, each proven with git diff, each restored to 53 of 53 green. The bounds refusals stayed green under the outcome mutation, so they are attributable to estimate.py's one bounds rule and not to this derivation. The tightness control is real: a legal optional edit and a record with no era and no note both validate clean, so the refusals are refusals of the mutation. The committed example is a fictional spec id (WARP-9402 is not in specs/) with an explicit EXAMPLE note, so nothing here fabricates a reconciliation of real work. One dead branch inside it (F6): load_dir's duplicate-spec message is unreachable, because read_record forces rec['spec'] to equal the filename stem, so two files in one directory can never both land under one key. That is a comment that reads as a live protection and is not one, but it is not a wrong answer.

Idempotence and the regrade refusal are separated by a driven pair, which is the right shape: with write_record's replace guard disabled exactly one row reds (the regrade refusal) while the idempotence row stays green, so writing the same measurement twice being free and rewriting a measurement being refused are two facts and not one flag. All four standdown reasons are driven in one pass with the paired control that the same specs DO reconcile once the corpus carries an integer actual, so the standdowns are the data's doing. Pairing is pure over injected collections and the date is a parameter, and I confirmed the double-pair identity holds. Nothing to add.

The honesty rule itself is sound and has teeth on both arms, and I verified that: accuracy([]) reporting measured True with a hit rate of 0 reds 3 rows with spend recorded and an empty ledger, render reporting a measured ledger as NOT MEASURED reds 1 row with a real record present, and error_pct_of returning 0 for an above-high actual reds 9 with a record present against 8 without. The remediation of the emptiness pins is real: I ran the sanctioned spend writer and then the sanctioned ledger writer and the suite stayed at 53 of 53 both times. Three things refute the criterion as written. First, the criterion's own text still requires an empty set over live state ('no recorded reconciliation in the tree is malformed'), which the suite spells as `_w1405_live_probs == []` at line 581, the one surviving empty-set live-state pin in the fragment: one present-but-malformed record takes CHECK_unit to 52 passed 1 failed, and AC5 of this same spec says a malformed record is named rather than blocking (F3). Second, the reddened row's label is about the EVENT LOG, so an operator whose record is malformed is told the wrong thing while the module's own `check` names the file and its nine problems correctly. Third, the surface this criterion calls inspectable prints a claim it never measured: the reconcile CLI's closing sentence asserts 'no shipped change carries a recorded actual' and cites WARP-1401's 0 percent spend coverage as 'this repository's measured state' on a branch entered for any reason at all, and one sanctioned spend.py record leaves that sentence byte-identical and false (F4). The reader-agreement clause is also toothless on a virgin tree by construction, which the fragment declares honestly and the criterion does not (F8): spend_for summing v // 2 reds 1 row with spend recorded and 0 without.

Most of this criterion is excellent and I could not break it. Leave-one-out really leaves one out and is asserted as an identity against a separate fit call, and ignoring the exclude argument reds exactly that one row and nothing else. The population pairing is the best work in the item: both of its declared mutations (paired_before over the whole ledger, and holdout dropping a never-fittable record instead of skipping it with a reason) red the one row that names the defect, and the mixed-fittability fixture spells out the 300 to 0 percent arithmetic the module must NOT publish. The era refusal, the minimum sample, the envelope-only-widens property and the width delta are all driven with their controls, and the never-labels claim is asserted over the strings a reader sees with a positive control that the matcher fires. What refutes the criterion is the floor. 'its range is the OBSERVED envelope of implied scales floored so that agreement cannot become false precision' is false in a region reachable with ordinary data, because the floor is applied to the SCALE and then _round_tokens(weight_tenths * scale // 10) recollapses the token bounds and nothing re-tests it. Driven end to end through five real specs, five real estimates, a real corpus, pair, fit and recalibrated_layer at the smallest structural weight estimate.py can produce (20 tenths) and a fitted scale of 1684: the shipped layer is 3000..4000, exactly ONE ROUND_STEP wide, a 33 percent spread, while its own recorded inputs say spread_floor_applied: yes and min_fitted_spread_pct: 50, and estimate.validate_record accepts it. That is verbatim the defect the spec says the floor was added to prevent. The check that names it drives ONE point (weight 100, fitted scale 75000) where rounding cannot bite, so it cannot fail for the defect its own criterion names (F2).

The load-bearing half is a genuine measurement and I confirmed it: the real validate.check_spec over a hermetic root returns the identical 0 with no record, a valid record and a malformed one, with a negative control that the same validator under the same root does refuse a genuinely broken spec, so a reconciliation provably cannot invalidate a spec. The present-but-broken path is measured over a real broken record rather than only over an absent directory, and replacing check_dir's validation loop with pass reds exactly that row. Two things refute the criterion. 'ADOPTION SAFE, AND NEVER A BLOCKER' is false at the gate: verify.sh declares CHECK_unit required, CHECK_unit is scripts/selftest.py, and one malformed reconciliation record turns it red (F3), so the module blocks through its own suite even though no gate stage calls it. And the NG5 clause's stated conclusion is false: the evidence is a substring scan over the module's own bytes, which the module does satisfy, but the sentence the suite and the module docstring draw from it ('so it cannot spawn a process or open a connection', headline 'NO CLOCK, NO SUBPROCESS, NO NETWORK') is contradicted by measurement. Wrapping subprocess.run and calling build_view(), the body of the `report` CLI, spawns 183 git processes in this repository, one `git log --all --grep` per spec plus `git show` per matching commit, reached through _repo_inputs into toe_corpus.git_touched (F5). Separately, the criterion cannot be assessed for an adopter at all today, because what an adopter receives is a module that crashes (F1).

findings.text: THE CODE UNDER REVIEW ALREADY SHIPS, AND IT SHIPS BROKEN. scripts/publish.py's EXCLUDE withholds engine/.veldo/estimate.py but does NOT withhold engine/.veldo/toe_reconcile.py, so this item's module is in the published set today while the module it cannot run without is not. Every function that touches _estimate() dies on an unhandled FileNotFoundError from importlib, because _mod() loads .veldo/estimate.py relative to the pack root. Three of the five subcommands fail, and they are the three that ARE the capability: report (the surface AC3 calls open to anyone), fit and reconcile all exit 1 with a raw traceback; only vocabulary and the empty-directory check survive. This is not a hypothetical about a future release: it is the state of publish.py at the commit I reviewed, and the same carve-out breaks engine/.veldo/toe_analogy.py and engine/.veldo/toe_budget.py, which also import estimate.py and are also published. CHECK_packaging installs all seven composed packs and reports 'adopter gate GREEN' without ever invoking this module, so no gate stage can see it. The comment above the EXCLUDE list explains that four modules are held back pending independent review; whoever wrote it did not notice that the three modules DEPENDING on one of the four were not held back with it. An adopter receives a fragment, and the fragment is the half that crashes.
findings.evidence: In the review copy: `python3 scripts/publish.py <dest>` -> 'publish: 420 file(s)', 'composed 7 pack(s)', 'leak scan clean'. publish.selected() over tracked_files(): engine/.veldo/toe_reconcile.py PUBLISHED, engine/.veldo/estimate.py WITHHELD, engine/.veldo/toe_analogy.py PUBLISHED, engine/.veldo/toe_budget.py PUBLISHED. `grep -l 'estimate.py' engine/.veldo/toe_*.py` -> toe_analogy.py, toe_budget.py, toe_reconcile.py. In <dest>/packs/claude: `ls .veldo/estimate.py` -> No such file or directory. Then [vocabulary] exit=0, [check] exit=0, [report] exit=1, [fit] exit=1, [reconcile --at 2026-08-13] exit=1, each of the three with 'FileNotFoundError: ... /packs/claude/.veldo/estimate.py' as the last stderr line. ADDITIVE CONTROL: copy the one withheld file in, change nothing else -> [report] exit=0 printing 'reconciliations: 0 record(s)' and 'accuracy: NOT MEASURED', the correct stand-down. Full transcript in WARP-1405-driven.txt, section F1.

findings.text: A REFITTED RANGE ONE ROUNDING STEP WIDE, RECORDING THAT THE FLOOR WAS APPLIED. recalibrated_range applies MIN_FITTED_SPREAD_PCT to the SCALE envelope and then converts to tokens through EST._round_tokens(weight_tenths * scale // 10); the rounding can recollapse the range and nothing re-tests the floor on the bounds actually produced. The only guard left is `if high <= low: high = low + ROUND_STEP`, which prevents collapse and not false precision. The result is the exact sentence the spec says the floor exists to refuse ('produced a range ONE ROUNDING STEP wide'), now with a layer whose own inputs assert spread_floor_applied: yes and min_fitted_spread_pct: 50 to a reader who recomputes it. It is reachable, not pathological: the trigger is a repository whose real cost per structural unit is well below the evidence-free declared prior of 25000, which is precisely the case the refit exists for, on small specs, which are the majority. And the check that names this cannot fail for it: the suite's floor assertion evaluates recalibrated_range at ONE point (weight 100, fitted scale 75000) where the bounds are hundreds of thousands of tokens and rounding is irrelevant, and the reproduce-from-inputs assertion follows the RECORDED spread_floor_applied flag and uses the same rounding, so both sides move together.
findings.evidence: Driven through the real pipeline, not a fixture: 5 specs at 1 AC / risk low / no footprint -> estimate.propose -> minimum structural_weight_tenths = 20 -> corpus rows at 1684 tokens per structural unit -> R.pair -> R.fit (fitted scale 1684, dispersion 0 percent, sample 5) -> R.recalibrated_layer. Layer: low=3000 high=4000, high-low=1000 = 1 ROUND_STEP, actual spread 33 percent, inputs spread_floor_applied='yes', min_fitted_spread_pct=50, and estimate.validate_record on a record carrying it returns CLEAN. Sweep over realistic weights 20..3000 x scales 200..200000: 1606759 floored cases, 146 violations of the declared floor, narrowest 25 percent at weight=26 scale=1684 (4000..5000). Contrast, same function: weight=100 scale=75000 -> 375000..750000, spread 100 percent, clears the floor, which is the only point the suite asks about. WARP-1405-driven.txt, section F2.

findings.text: THE ONE SURVIVING EMPTY-SET LIVE-STATE PIN, AND IT MAKES THE MODULE A BLOCKER UNDER A LABEL ABOUT SOMETHING ELSE. The fragment's spend and ledger emptiness pins were remediated and the remediation works, which I verified by running both sanctioned writers. What was left behind is `_w1405_live_probs == []` at line 581, required by AC3's own text ('no recorded reconciliation in the tree is malformed'). It is an assertion whose required answer is an empty set over live data, and one malformed record in .veldo/reconciliations reddens CHECK_unit, which verify.sh declares required. So a spec whose AC5 is titled 'ADOPTION SAFE, AND NEVER A BLOCKER' and whose module correctly names a broken record instead of dropping it has a suite that turns that same broken record into a red gate. Two criteria of one spec disagree. The harm is sharper than the contradiction: the row that reddens is 'AC3 MEASURED OVER THE REAL EVENT LOG', so the operator is told the event-log measurement failed when what actually happened is that a reconciliation record is malformed, which the module's own `check` reports correctly and by name. This is also outside the reach of the one stage built to catch pins: check_first_use.py declares that it 'only fills the corpora its mutation table fills', and its table covers spend alone, so no sanctioned-writer run can reach a malformed record. The fix is one line: assert that load_dir NAMES each problem it found, not that there are none.
findings.evidence: Wrote .veldo/reconciliations/WARP-0100.yaml containing only schema, spec and actual. `python3 .veldo/toe_reconcile.py check` -> '1 record(s) checked, 9 problem(s)' naming the file per problem, which is correct. `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 15_warp_1405_reconciliation` -> 'selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 78 passed, 1 failed', the failed row being 'WARP-1405 AC3 MEASURED OVER THE REAL EVENT LOG ...'. Baseline on the same tree is 79 passed 0 failed. `grep -n '_w1405_live_probs == \[\]'` -> line 581, and it is the only clause in the fragment requiring an empty answer over live state. verify.sh line 19: CHECK_unit="required:python3 scripts/selftest.py". WARP-1405-driven.txt, section F3.

findings.text: THE RECONCILE CLI STATES A SPEND MEASUREMENT IT DID NOT TAKE, AND SHIPS A CLAIM ABOUT THIS REPOSITORY TO EVERY ADOPTER. _cli's `if not recs:` branch prints 'nothing to reconcile: %d committed estimate(s), and no shipped change carries a recorded actual. That is this repository's measured state (WARP-1401 measured 0 percent spend coverage), not a failure'. The branch is entered whenever the derived record list is empty, which in this tree is because there are ZERO committed estimates, and on that path the spend predicate is never consulted at all. So the second clause is a confident zero over an input the code never read on that path, and the third clause is a dated finding about the author's repository asserted as the reader's. It is the one place in the whole item where the module does exactly what the item exists to refuse: reports 0 where nothing was measured. The same defect is in the shipped module docstring, which pins '904 events, 148 shipped specs, 95.3 percent cycle coverage and 0 PERCENT SPEND COVERAGE' and then states 'THE LEDGER IS EMPTY' as a property of the reader's repository; two of those figures are already stale in this tree. Nothing in the suite asserts over either string, which is why they drifted. This is user-visible output, it ships, and an adopter installing the pack is told a fact about somebody else's data.
findings.evidence: Virgin tree: `python3 .veldo/toe_reconcile.py reconcile --at 2026-08-13` -> 'nothing to reconcile: 0 committed estimate(s), and no shipped change carries a recorded actual. That is this repository's measured state (WARP-1401 measured 0 percent spend coverage), not a failure'. Then one sanctioned `python3 .veldo/spend.py record --spec WARP-0100 --basis harness_reported --tokens 750000`; toe_corpus.spend_for(metrics.load(), 'WARP-0100') -> {'tokens': 750000, 'cost_usd': 0.0, 'human_minutes': 0, 'spend_recorded': True}; the same command prints the byte-identical sentence. Docstring figures re-measured over today's bytes: 1191 events (docstring 904) and 174 shipped specs (docstring 148). WARP-1405-driven.txt, section F4.

findings.text: AN ABSENCE PROVEN BY A SUBSTRING SCAN, STANDING IN FOR A PROPERTY OF THE CALL GRAPH, AND THE CONCLUSION IS FALSE. AC5's NG5 check is `all(tok not in <module source> for tok in ('import subprocess', 'import socket', 'import urllib', 'Popen(', 'datetime.now', 'time.time'))`. The literal claim holds: the module names none of them. The claim the suite and the module then make from it does not. The suite's label says 'THE MODULE REACHES FOR NOTHING OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY ... so it cannot spawn a process or open a connection (NG5)' and the module's own shipped docstring headlines 'NO CLOCK, NO SUBPROCESS, NO NETWORK'. build_view(), which is the entire body of the `report` CLI, reaches toe_corpus.git_touched through _repo_inputs and spawns one `git log --all --grep <spec>` per spec plus a `git show` per matching commit. Measured by wrapping subprocess.run: 183 spawns for one `report` in this repository. So a stranger reads a false statement in the module they installed, and gets an O(specs) fan-out of git invocations from a surface documented as pure reading. The correctness of the READS-ONLY claim is not in question; the process claim is, and a scan of one file's bytes can never carry it. Note this makes the finding about the CHECK and the PROSE, not about a wrong number: the fix is to state the true property (the module itself imports none of these; its dependencies shell out to git) or to measure the call graph.
findings.evidence: python3, wrapping subprocess.run before loading the module: 'import subprocess' in the module source -> False; then build_view() -> 183 subprocess.run calls, first three [['git','log','--format=%H','--grep','WARP-0100','--all'], ... 'WARP-0101' ..., ... 'WARP-0102' ...]. Call path: toe_reconcile._repo_inputs -> toe_corpus.build -> files_touched -> git_touched -> _run(['git', ...]); toe_corpus.py line 39 'import subprocess', line 159 the git log. Module docstring lines 73 to 75 carry the headline. WARP-1405-driven.txt, section F5.

findings.text: UNREACHABLE PROTECTION READING AS A LIVE ONE. load_dir carries a duplicate-spec guard ('two records claim spec %r') that can never fire: read_record defaults spec_id to path.stem and validate_record refuses any record whose `spec` differs from it, so every entry load_dir adds is keyed by a distinct filename stem. Two files in one directory both declaring the same spec are both refused as misfiled long before the duplicate check is reached. Harmless as behaviour, but it is a branch a reader will count as a defence that exists.
findings.evidence: Two files A.yaml and B.yaml in one temp directory, both containing 'spec: A': load_dir -> 2 problems, and `any('two records claim' in p for p in probs)` is False; both problems are the filename-is-the-key refusal. WARP-1405-driven.txt, section F6.

findings.text: A CLAUSE THAT CANNOT FAIL, INSIDE THE ITEM'S MOST IMPORTANT ASSERTION. Line 582 of the fragment requires `sorted(_w1405_live_ledger) == sorted(_r['spec'] for _r in _w1405_live_recs)`, comparing a dict's keys against the `spec` field of that dict's own values. load_dir keys by exactly that field, so the two enumerations are one enumeration and the equality is true by construction. It sits inside the AC3 live-measurement conjunction, where it reads as a partition check and contributes nothing.
findings.evidence: python3: led={'X':{'spec':'X'},'Y':{'spec':'Y'}}; recs=R.ordered(list(led.values())); sorted(led)==sorted(r['spec'] for r in recs) -> True, and load_dir's only insertion is out[rec['spec']] = rec. WARP-1405-driven.txt, section F7.

findings.text: AC3 PRESENTS A CLAUSE WITH NO TEETH ON A VIRGIN TREE AS A LIVE MEASUREMENT. The criterion says 'the raw spend predicate and toe_corpus's own reader AGREE over every spec id that log names on which of them carry tokens, cost_usd or human_minutes and on the figures themselves'. Today both sides of the set equality are empty and the re-summation is 143 instances of 0 == 0, so no reader defect can be detected. The fragment's docstring states this plainly for mutation 17; the criterion does not, and the criterion is what a later reader will cite. I confirmed it in both directions rather than taking either at its word. Recorded as minor because it is disclosed and because the clause gains real teeth the moment any spend exists, which is the trade the remediation deliberately made.
findings.evidence: spend_for mutated to sum `v // 2` in both toe_corpus copies, diff proving it landed. With one sanctioned spend recorded: 78 passed 1 failed, the red row being the AC3 live event-log arm. On the virgin tree with the identical mutation: 79 passed 0 failed. WARP-1405-driven.txt, mutations M17 and M17-bis.

findings.text: THE ONE WIRING POINT IS ONLY PARTLY ROOTED. _repo_inputs(root) threads its root into estimate.load_dir(root=base) and toe_corpus.build(specs_dir=base / 'specs') but calls metrics.load() and policy_check.protected_patterns() with no root, and neither takes one. So build_view(root=X) reads THIS repository's event log and THIS repository's protected-path policy while reading X's specs and estimates. The suite copies policy.yaml into its viewroot, which suggests the author expected it to be read from there. It is harmless today because the fixture root carries no specs, so the corpus comes out empty either way, but AC3's measured branch rests on figures being 'internally reproducible' and the seam that would let anyone check that over a controlled root is not hermetic. It is also the seam an adopter test would need.
findings.evidence: toe_reconcile.py lines 1394 to 1396: EST.load_dir(root=base) / C.build(specs_dir=base / 'specs', events=M.load(), protected=PC.protected_patterns()). metrics.py line 121 'def load():' and policy_check.py line 50 'def protected_patterns():', neither taking a root. WARP-1405-driven.txt, section F9.

findings.text: THE SPEC DECLARES NO FALSIFICATION AT ALL. specs/WARP-1405-reconciliation-and-estimator-accuracy.md contains zero falsified_by clauses, while specs/TEMPLATE.md carries the field and 45 of the 213 specs in this corpus declare it, and the contract's own falsification migration counts this spec among the 168 stood down. The item's declared falsifications exist only as 17 numbered mutations in the suite's module docstring, which is prose with no reader that can refresh it. That is enough for a reviewer who reads the fragment, and I drove all 17 and all 17 had teeth, so this is a form finding and not a substance one. But it means the falsification for the criterion this review refutes on arithmetic (AC4's floor) was never written where the migration could ever ask about it.

Gate output at HEAD: 'falsified_by STANDS DOWN ... 45 spec(s) declare behaviour of 213, 45 already comply, 0 would be refused, 168 stood down. Posture: REFUSING since 2026-08-11'. summary: SHIP VERDICT: do-not-ship. FAIL on one blocker and four majors. The blocker is not about the module's own quality, it is about what is already leaving the building: scripts/publish.py withholds engine/.veldo/estimate.py from the published tree but does NOT withhold engine/.veldo/toe_reconcile.py, so this item's module is in every composed pack today and cannot run there. Measured in a real publish: report, fit and reconcile all exit 1 with a raw FileNotFoundError traceback, and only vocabulary and an empty-directory check survive. The additive control settles the cause: put the one withheld file back, change nothing else, and report prints the correct stand-down and exits 0. The same carve-out breaks toe_analogy.py and toe_budget.py, and CHECK_packaging installs all seven packs, reports 'adopter gate GREEN', and never invokes any of them. Whoever held four modules back for review did not hold back the three that import one of them. The second reason not to ship is a wrong answer in the exact place a criterion promises protection. AC4's floor is applied to the fitted SCALE and then _round_tokens recollapses the token bounds, so at the smallest structural weight estimate.py can produce and a fitted scale below the evidence-free declared prior, the shipped layer is 3000..4000, one ROUND_STEP wide, a 33 percent spread, while its own recorded inputs say spread_floor_applied: yes and min_fitted_spread_pct: 50, and estimate.validate_record accepts it. That is verbatim the false precision the spec says the floor was added to prevent, it is reachable with ordinary small specs and a cheap model, and the assertion that names it evaluates one point in the input space where rounding cannot bite. 146 violations in a sweep over realistic weights. Three more majors are honesty defects rather than arithmetic ones: the one surviving empty-set live-state pin makes a malformed record redden CHECK_unit under a row labelled about the event log, which contradicts this spec's own AC5 and misdirects the operator; the reconcile CLI prints 'no shipped change carries a recorded actual' plus a dated claim about THIS repository on a branch where it never consulted the spend predicate, byte-identically unchanged after a sanctioned spend.py record, and the module docstring's pinned 904 events and 148 shipped specs are already 1191 and 174; and the NG5 conclusion 'so it cannot spawn a process' is false, measured at 183 git spawns for one report. WHAT IS GOOD, and it is a lot: I drove all 17 declared falsifications, applied to both module copies, each proven with git diff, each restored, and 17 of 17 had teeth on the rows they named, with the two live-arm counts reproducing exactly in the state the docstring names. AC1 and AC2 are confirmed without reservation. The population pairing in AC4 and the three-way check_spec measurement in AC5 are the strongest work I have reviewed in this codebase, and the emptiness remediation genuinely holds: both sanctioned writers ran and the suite stayed 53 of 53. This item is close. It is not shippable while its published form crashes and its floor does not floor.
